description: The aim of this course is to familiarize students with the analysis and design of basic transistor amplifier circuits, oscillators and wave-shaping circuits.

syllabus.title: Amplifier Models and AC Analysis
syllabus.body: Voltage amplifier, current amplifier, transconductance amplifier and transresistance amplifier. Biasing schemes for BJT and FET amplifiers, bias stability, various configurations such as CE/CS, CB/CG and CC/CD and their features, small-signal analysis, low-frequency transistor models, estimation of voltage gain, input resistance and output resistance, design procedure for particular specifications, and low-frequency analysis of multistage amplifiers.

syllabus.title: Multistage Amplifiers and Power Amplifiers
syllabus.body: High-frequency transistor models, frequency response of single-stage and multistage amplifiers, cascode amplifier. Various classes of operation including Class A, B, AB and C, comparison of their power efficiency, types of distortion and linearity issues. Voltage regulators: discrete transistor voltage regulation, series and shunt voltage regulators.

syllabus.title: Op-Amp and Its Applications
syllabus.body: Differential amplifier basic structure and principle of operation, calculation of differential gain, common-mode gain, CMRR and ICMR. Op-amp design for a given specification. Applications including inverting and non-inverting amplifiers, integrator and differentiator, summing amplifier, precision rectifier, Schmitt trigger and its applications. Feedback concepts and types, practical feedback circuits, transfer gain, general characteristics of negative-feedback amplifiers, input resistance, output resistance, feedback topologies including voltage series, current series, voltage shunt and current shunt, and effect of feedback on gain and bandwidth.

syllabus.title: Oscillators and Wave Shaping Circuits
syllabus.body: Basic concept of oscillators, Barkhausen criterion, RC oscillators including phase-shift and Wien bridge oscillators, LC oscillators including Hartley, Colpitts and Clapp oscillators, non-sinusoidal oscillators and frequency stability. Multivibrators including astable, monostable and bistable circuits. High-pass and low-pass filters using RC, RL and RLC circuits and their response to step, pulse, square and ramp inputs, attenuators. Active low-pass, high-pass, band-pass and band-stop filters and design guidelines. Digital-to-analog converters, analog-to-digital converters and case studies of practical circuits in typical electronic systems.

outcomes: Acquire knowledge of single-stage, cascaded and feedback amplifier configurations and frequency response characteristics of BJT and FET circuits.
Analyze the performance of op-amp, power amplifier and oscillator circuits.
Analyze various filter and multivibrator circuits.
Apply the knowledge gained in the design of transistorized circuits, amplifiers and oscillators.
textbooks: J. Millman and C. C. Halkias, "Integrated Electronics", Tata McGraw Hill, 2007.
J. Millman and H. Taub, "Pulse, Digital and Switching Waveforms", Tata McGraw Hill, 2007.
Robert L. Boylestad and Louis Nashelsky, "Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory", Pearson, 10th Edition, 2012.
referenceBooks: Adel S. Sedra and Kenneth C. Smith, "Microelectronic Circuits: Theory and Application", 5th Edition.
Behzad Razavi, "Fundamentals of Microelectronics", John Wiley.
